message.content:
For **`contentEditable`** there isn’t a single “boolean” flag – the attribute itself accepts one of three literal strings: | Value | Meaning | |-------|---------| | `true` | Element is fully editable (markup may be entered) | | `false` | Editing disabled | | `plaintext‑only` | Element is editable *but* only plain‑text input is accepted | So if your code receives `"plaintext‑only"` you don’t need to translate it into `"true"` or `"false"`. Just set the attribute exactly to that string: ```html
…
``` If you’re calling the helper function `convertEnumeratedValue`, passing `{ key: "contenteditable", value: "plaintext-only" }` will simply leave the value untouched—because `"plaintext-only"` is an officially supported enum member. Only values like empty string (`""`) or `"false"` would normally map back to `"false"`, while anything else maps to `"true"`. Bottom line: **use `"plaintext-only"` verbatim—it’s already a valid, semantically meaningful value for the `contenteditable` attribute.**
